answer: Each agent receives a scarce, nontransferable admission credential only after completing a costly proof-of-work challenge, with the difficulty adjusted as demand rises. The credential expires, so an attacker cannot cheaply stockpile identities. Inlet nodes verify the challenge and reject reused credentials before agents can claim rewards; shale records make issuance auditable, while an oasis of free identities never forms. The attacker pays in compute, electricity, and time for every identity, and must keep paying to renew it.
